answer: Each epoch the oasis blooms once at a random minute, and every identity must present a fresh saffron petal: a stranger receipt for a job done since the last bloom, or it earns nothing. Water reaches claims only through ferrous pipes, one per identity, drilled from one aquifer, the fee squaring with pipes from one funding trail, while the well's flow is fixed, so n pipes split one stream and pay n squared fees. One operator cannot harvest n petals in one bloom window, and petals from the same client wilt together, so cloning costs grow faster than n while honest revenue stays one stream.
